newsitem.title: FRANCE: French troops board ship ready for Albania.
newsitem.headline: French troops board ship ready for Albania.

text.p: More than 400 French troops boarded a ship on Thursday ready to leave for Albania, the first part of a 1,000-strong French contingent in an Italian-led force to the battered state.

The troops boarded the 150-metre long Orage landing ship in the Mediterranean port of Toulon and were awaiting a formal green light from Rome to depart on Friday. The remaining 600 or so would travel by a specially-chartered ferry.
"A meeting is going on in Rome right now at which the final details of the intervention will be worked out," a Defence Ministry official said.

The French troops, part of a U.N.-approved force of up to 6,000 soldiers, aim to disembark at the northern port of Durres and secure the road to Tirana, about 40 km (25 miles) east for supplies of food and medicines.
The French contingent includes wheeled tanks, armoured personnel carriers and two Puma transport helicopters. All units have experience of foreign missions, notably in former Yugoslavia.
The French force should be completely operational 13 days after disembarcation in Albania, where anger at failed savings schemes this year spilled over into an armed insurrection.
The security force is due to begin arriving in Albania on Monday. Italy is planning to send about 2,000 soldiers, Greece 600, Spain 300, Turkey 600 and Romania 300.
